title: Positive-degree Zariski cohomology classes vanish locally
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal G$ be an abelian sheaf on the small Zariski site $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-sc-zariski-site]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ let $\mathcal G|_U$ be the abelian sheaf $W\mapsto\mathcal G(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) on $U_{\rm Zar}$. Let $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ be any injective resolution of $\mathcal G$ in the abelian category $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], so that $H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\mathcal G)=H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))$ [def-sc-zariski-cohomology]; by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-open-restriction-injectives], $\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$ is an injective resolution of $\mathcal G|_U$ in $\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ with $\Gamma(U,\mathcal I^\bullet|_U)=\mathcal I^\bullet(U)$, so $H^q(U_{\rm Zar},\mathcal G|_U)=H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U))$, and the restriction $\xi\mapsto\xi|_U$, $H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\mathcal G)\to H^q(U_{\rm Zar},\mathcal G|_U)$, is the map induced on $H^q$ by the morphism of complexes $\mathcal I^\bullet(X)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(U)$ given by the restriction maps of the sheaves $\mathcal I^p$. Then for every integer $q>0$, every class $\xi\in H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\mathcal G)$ and every point $x\in X$ there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ such that $\xi|_U=0$ in $H^q(U_{\rm Zar},\mathcal G|_U)$.

proof.text: *A cocycle representing $\xi$.* By [def-sc-zariski-cohomology] and [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2), applied to the site $X_{\rm Zar}$ and its object $X$, $H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\mathcal G)=H^q(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))=\operatorname{Ker}(d^q_X:\mathcal I^q(X)\to\mathcal I^{q+1}(X))/\operatorname{Im}(d^{q-1}_X:\mathcal I^{q-1}(X)\to\mathcal I^q(X))$, where $d^p_W$ is the component at $W$ of the differential $d^p:\mathcal I^p\to\mathcal I^{p+1}$ (here $q-1\ge0$, so $\mathcal I^{q-1}$ is a term of the resolution). Choose $s\in\mathcal I^q(X)$ with $d^q_X(s)=0$ whose class is $\xi$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 01FW (label lemma-kill-cohomology-class-on-covering), line 714, and its proof

proof.text: *The complex of sheaves is exact in degree $q$.* Since $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution, the cohomology of $\mathcal I^\bullet$ is concentrated in degree $0$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; as $q>0$, the complex $\mathcal I^{q-1}\xrightarrow{d^{q-1}}\mathcal I^q\xrightarrow{d^q}\mathcal I^{q+1}$ of the abelian category $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ is exact at $\mathcal I^q$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Let $\mathcal K$ be the kernel of $d^q$ in $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$; by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (1) it is the sectionwise kernel, $\mathcal K(W)=\operatorname{Ker}(d^q_W)\subseteq\mathcal I^q(W)$ with the restriction maps of $\mathcal I^q$, and the kernel morphism $k:\mathcal K\to\mathcal I^q$ is the inclusion. Since $d^q\circ d^{q-1}=0$, $d^{q-1}$ factors as $k\circ d'$ with $d':\mathcal I^{q-1}\to\mathcal K$, $d'_W(t)=d^{q-1}_W(t)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift], exactness at $\mathcal I^q$ means that $d'$ is an epimorphism of $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$.

source.place: Lemma 01FW proof: 'the complex I^bullet is exact in degree n. Hence Im(I^{n-1} -> I^n) = Ker(I^n -> I^{n+1}) as sheaves'

proof.text: *$s$ is locally a coboundary.* By step 1, $s\in\mathcal K(X)$. The small Zariski site $X_{\rm Zar}$ is a site [def-sc-zariski-site], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1), so [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] applies to the epimorphism $d'$ of step 2 and the section $s\in\mathcal K(X)$: there are a covering $\{V_j\subseteq X\}_{j\in J}$ of $X$ in $X_{\rm Zar}$ and sections $t_j\in\mathcal I^{q-1}(V_j)$ with $d^{q-1}_{V_j}(t_j)=d'_{V_j}(t_j)=s|_{V_j}$ (restriction in $\mathcal K$ is restriction in $\mathcal I^q$). A covering of $X$ in $X_{\rm Zar}$ is a family of opens whose union is $X$ [def-sc-zariski-site], so $x\in V_j$ for some $j$. Put $U=V_j$ and $t=t_j$: $U$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ and $d^{q-1}_U(t)=s|_U$.

source.place: Lemma 01FW proof: 'Since tilde xi is a section of the kernel sheaf over U we conclude there exists a covering {U_i -> U} of the site such that tilde xi|_{U_i} is the image under d of a section xi_i in I^{n-1}(U_i)'

proof.text: *The restriction of $\xi$ to $U$ vanishes.* By [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-open-restriction-injectives] (3), $\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$ is an injective resolution in $\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ and $\Gamma(U,\mathcal I^\bullet|_U)=\mathcal I^\bullet(U)$, so $H^q(U_{\rm Zar},\mathcal G|_U)=H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U))$ [def-sc-zariski-cohomology]. The restriction maps $\mathcal I^p(X)\to\mathcal I^p(U)$ commute with the differentials ($d^p$ is a morphism of sheaves), so they form a morphism of complexes, and by the definition of the restriction in the statement $\xi|_U$ is the class of the cocycle $s|_U\in\mathcal I^q(U)$. By step 3, $s|_U=d^{q-1}_U(t)$ lies in $\operatorname{Im}(d^{q-1}_U)$, so its class in $H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U))$ is $0$, i.e. $\xi|_U=0$. Since the resolution was arbitrary, this holds for every choice of injective resolution used to define the restriction.
